question: Which self-supervised objective yields representations of spatiotemporal physical simulations that best preserve governing-parameter information, and do latent-prediction representations transfer more effectively than masked-pixel reconstruction or autoregressive surrogate representations?

key_findings.claim: A dynamics-oriented JEPA produces lower governing-parameter regression error than a separately trained VideoMAE on all three tested physical systems.
key_findings.evidence: After 100-epoch attentive-probe training on frozen encoders, JEPA versus VideoMAE mean-squared errors are 0.079 versus 0.160 on active matter, 0.38 versus 0.67 on shear flow, and 0.13 versus 0.18 on Rayleigh-Bénard convection. The authors summarize these as relative error reductions of 51%, 43%, and 28% respectively.

anchors.section: Table 1 / JEPAs outperform MAE in parameter estimation

key_findings.claim: The JEPA result does not establish that generic latent prediction is superior to all physics-specific modeling: the DISCO representation is best on every system.
key_findings.evidence: DISCO's MSE is 0.057 on active matter, 0.13 on shear flow, and 0.01 on Rayleigh-Bénard, compared with JEPA's 0.079, 0.38, and 0.13. The active-matter results are relatively close, but DISCO is roughly 2.9 times lower error on shear flow and 13 times lower on Rayleigh-Bénard.

anchors.section: Table 1 / Comparison with methods for physical modeling

key_findings.claim: The autoregressive MPP baseline transfers inconsistently to parameter regression despite full end-to-end fine-tuning.
key_findings.evidence: MPP obtains MSE 0.230 on active matter and 0.59 on shear flow, both worse than JEPA, but 0.08 on Rayleigh-Bénard, better than JEPA's 0.13 and VideoMAE's 0.18. MPP is the only model fine-tuned end to end because its pretraining excluded all three target datasets, so the comparison also changes pretraining exposure and adaptation protocol.

key_findings.claim: On shear-flow parameter prediction, JEPA remains more sample-efficient than VideoMAE over the three labeled-data fractions reported.
key_findings.evidence: At 10%, 50%, and 100% of the fine-tuning data, JEPA MSE is 0.57, 0.40, and 0.38, versus VideoMAE's 0.98, 0.75, and 0.67. The 50% split contains 16,000 examples; JEPA with 10% of labels (0.57) is better than VideoMAE with all labels (0.67).

anchors.section: Table 2 / JEPA exhibits desirable scaling behavior

key_findings.claim: The benchmark evaluates recoverability of two governing parameters per system, not general physical understanding.
key_findings.evidence: The probe predicts active dipole strength and steric-alignment strength for active matter, Reynolds and Schmidt numbers for shear flow, and Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers for convection. The paper uses average two-parameter MSE as a quantifiable proxy for physical information, without testing rollout, conservation, stability, phase classification, control, or out-of-distribution regimes.

key_findings.claim: The comparison groups methods by latent-versus-pixel prediction, but objective is confounded with architecture, representation shape, target-specific exposure, and fine-tuning protocol.
key_findings.evidence: JEPA is a 3D ConvNeXt-style CNN with a 128-channel spatial output and VICReg regularization; VideoMAE is a ViT-tiny/16 with a time-resolved 384-channel output; DISCO supplies a 1x384 hypernetwork embedding pretrained on The Well; MPP supplies 192-channel spatial embeddings from published weights and is fine-tuned end to end. Separate JEPA and VideoMAE models are pretrained for only six epochs on each target dataset, whereas the physical baselines use prior multi-physics pretraining.

key_findings.claim: The data support a narrow conclusion that latent-prediction models occupy the top two rows of this particular parameter-regression comparison, not a causal conclusion about objective class.
key_findings.evidence: JEPA and DISCO are the two latent-prediction methods and are first and second on the three systems, whereas VideoMAE and MPP predict pixels. But there is no same-backbone objective ablation, matched pretraining budget, random-encoder control, statistical uncertainty, or time-shuffling test, so architecture and protocol alternatives remain viable explanations.

anchors.section: Comparison with methods for physical modeling

method.core_idea: Use downstream regression of known governing parameters as a quantitative probe of whether a self-supervised physical-dynamics representation retains scientifically relevant information, then compare latent prediction, masked-pixel reconstruction, autoregressive pretraining, and in-context operator inference on the same three simulation families.
method.mechanism: The proposed JEPA encodes one k-frame segment with a 3D ConvNeXt-style encoder and predicts the latent representation of the following k-frame segment. A VICReg loss combines invariance between predicted and target latents with variance and covariance regularizers to prevent collapse. VideoMAE reconstructs masked spatiotemporal pixels. DISCO's pretrained hypernetwork output and MPP's pretrained AViT-tiny features serve as physics-specific baselines. All inputs contain 16 frames. Frozen JEPA, VideoMAE, and DISCO encoders receive 100-epoch attentive regression probes, while MPP is fine-tuned end to end. Performance is average MSE over two parameters on each of active matter, shear flow, and Rayleigh-Bénard convection from The Well.
assumptions: Low supervised error on two governing parameters is an adequate proxy for the physical relevance of a representation.
The target parameters are not recoverable mainly from static appearance, grid artifacts, normalization statistics, or other shortcuts unrelated to temporal dynamics.
Average MSE over two parameters is meaningful even though the extraction does not specify target scaling or normalization.
Frozen attentive-probe performance is comparable across representations with substantially different spatial, temporal, and channel shapes.
End-to-end MPP adaptation can be interpreted alongside frozen-encoder probes despite the different optimization capacity.

Pretraining exposure is comparable enough to group outcomes by latent-versus-pixel objective, although DISCO is pretrained on The Well, MPP excludes the target systems, and JEPA/VideoMAE are target-specific.
Six pretraining epochs are sufficient for a fair comparison between the custom JEPA and VideoMAE implementations.

techniques.role: Quantifies retained physical information by predicting known simulation parameters from learned representations.
Predicts the representation of the next k-frame window from the preceding k-frame window rather than reconstructing pixels.
Combines invariance, per-dimension variance, and off-diagonal covariance penalties in JEPA pretraining.
Trains a learnable attention-based regression head while holding JEPA, VideoMAE, and DISCO encoders fixed.
Places generic latent and pixel SSL models beside autoregressive and operator-learning physics models.
Measures parameter-regression error at 10%, 50%, and 100% of shear-flow labels.
Trains separate JEPA and VideoMAE models for each physical system to specialize the learned representation.

evaluations.setting: Active-matter trajectories from The Well; regression of active dipole strength alpha and steric-alignment strength zeta
evaluations.baseline: Masked-pixel SSL plus two physics-specific pretrained models

evaluations.setting: Shear-flow trajectories from The Well; regression of Reynolds and Schmidt numbers
evaluations.baseline: Masked-pixel SSL plus two physics-specific pretrained models

evaluations.setting: Rayleigh-Bénard trajectories from The Well; regression of Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers
evaluations.baseline: Masked-pixel SSL plus two physics-specific pretrained models; both physical models outperform JEPA here

evaluations.setting: Shear-flow attentive probing with 10%, 50%, and 100% labeled subsets; 50% equals 16,000 examples
evaluations.baseline: Same method at full labels and the alternative SSL objective at matched label fractions

evaluations.result: JEPA l/16 x w/16 x 128; VideoMAE l/16 x w/16 x t/2 x 384; DISCO 1 x 384; MPP l/16 x w/16 x 192; JEPA/VideoMAE pretrain six epochs and all downstream training lasts 100 epochs
evaluations.baseline: No architecture- or compute-matched objective ablation

limitations: Reviewer-identified: the paper has no dedicated limitations section and reports no seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, or variance over pretraining and probing runs.

Reviewer-identified: the proposed objective comparison is confounded by a 3D ConvNeXt-style JEPA versus a transformer VideoMAE, different output shapes, and potentially different parameter counts and optimization behavior.

Reviewer-identified: DISCO, MPP, and the target-specific SSL models have different pretraining corpora and target exposure; DISCO is pretrained on The Well while MPP explicitly excludes the evaluated systems.
Reviewer-identified: MPP is adapted end to end, while the other encoders are frozen; this is neither a controlled representation probe nor a controlled fine-tuning comparison.
Reviewer-identified: governing-parameter regression is only one type of downstream task and need not predict rollout accuracy, stability, conservation, control utility, or scientific discovery value.

Reviewer-identified: a parameter may be visible through stationary textures, field amplitudes, boundary conditions, or preprocessing statistics, so low error need not demonstrate learning of temporal physical dynamics.
Reviewer-identified: the paper does not report static-frame, frame-order-shuffle, shortened-context, random-encoder, or hand-engineered-summary baselines that would reveal such shortcuts.
Reviewer-identified: six pretraining epochs may undertrain VideoMAE differently from JEPA; there is no learning-curve, compute, wall-time, or convergence comparison.
Reviewer-identified: target normalization and the scale of each parameter are not specified, making the average two-parameter MSE difficult to interpret and potentially dominated by one parameter.
Reviewer-identified: the attentive probe is not a linear probe and its capacity is not detailed, so it can learn nonlinear summaries that obscure what is directly encoded.

Reviewer-identified: DISCO is better on all three systems and MPP is better on Rayleigh-Bénard, so the conclusion that latent prediction 'consistently' produces more physically informative representations must be scoped to this grouped, confounded comparison rather than every model/task pairing.
failure_modes: If a governing parameter changes visual scale or stationary texture, the probe may exploit a shortcut and overstate temporal understanding.
If field normalization removes parameter-dependent magnitude, performance rankings may change sharply because different encoders rely on different cues.
The target-specific JEPA may not transfer to a new PDE family, parameter range, resolution, boundary condition, or set of physical fields.
A frozen attentive probe may favor spatial-token representations over a single global DISCO vector or temporally resolved VideoMAE tokens because aggregation capacity is not matched.
Autoregressive MPP features may be useful for rollout yet poor for parameter regression, so this probe can rank representations opposite to their intended use.
A six-epoch run can make optimization speed look like objective superiority even when longer VideoMAE training would close the gap.
MSE averaged across differently scaled parameters can hide failure on one parameter while being dominated by the other.
A representation that predicts in-distribution parameters can fail to interpolate or extrapolate outside the training parameter grid.
Architectural effects attributed to latent prediction may disappear under a same-backbone JEPA-versus-pixel reconstruction comparison.
The method may discard fine-scale fields needed for scientific tasks other than global parameter identification.
reusable_insights: Evaluate scientific representations on explicit downstream quantities rather than assuming low rollout or reconstruction error implies useful scientific abstraction.
Separate representation quality from generative fidelity: a model can be weak at pixels yet retain a compact statistic useful for inference.
Use label-fraction curves, not only full-data probes, because a useful representation should reduce the labeled-data burden.
Include both generic SSL and domain-specific operator/surrogate baselines; neither class should be presumed superior by design.
For causal claims about objectives, hold backbone, tokenization, pretraining examples, optimizer, compute, and probe capacity constant.
Add static-frame and shuffled-time controls to determine whether a purported dynamics representation actually uses temporal evolution.
Report each physical parameter separately and normalize transparently before averaging regression errors.
open_questions: Does JEPA retain its advantage over pixel reconstruction with the same architecture, parameter count, data order, compute budget, and convergence criterion?
How much parameter-prediction accuracy remains with one frame, shuffled frames, reversed time, or only simple field statistics?
Do the representations generalize to unseen parameter ranges, grids, resolutions, boundary conditions, system families, and noisy or partial observations?
Are parameter-regression rankings correlated with rollout stability, conservation-law error, qualitative regime classification, inverse problems, and downstream control?
Which VICReg term and which temporal offset are responsible for the JEPA gain?
How do linear probes, capacity-matched nonlinear probes, full fine-tuning, and few-shot Bayesian decoders alter the ranking?
Why does DISCO outperform JEPA by an order of magnitude on Rayleigh-Bénard but not on active matter?
Can a multi-physics JEPA combine DISCO's cross-system operator inference with the sample efficiency of target-specific latent prediction?
What information is lost by each representation even when aggregate parameter MSE is low?

competitive_landscape.title: Self-Supervised Learning with Lie Symmetries for Partial Differential Equations
competitive_landscape.difference: Mialon et al. already apply joint-embedding SSL to heterogeneous PDE data, inject known Lie-point symmetries as augmentations, and evaluate PDE-coefficient regression as well as neural-solver improvement. The present paper removes the symmetry-specific augmentation, introduces a consecutive-window VICReg/JEPA implementation on three The Well systems, and focuses on a four-way latent-versus-pixel representation benchmark; it is not the first JEPA-style physical representation or governing-parameter probe.

competitive_landscape.title: DISCO: learning to DISCover an evolution Operator for multi-physics-agnostic prediction
competitive_landscape.difference: DISCO uses a large hypernetwork to infer a trajectory-specific evolution operator from a short context and explicitly integrates that operator for future-state prediction. The current study reuses the hypernetwork output as a frozen embedding for parameter regression; DISCO wins all three tables, making it both a strong baseline and evidence that physics-oriented latent operator inference can exceed the custom JEPA.

competitive_landscape.title: Multiple Physics Pretraining for Physical Surrogate Models
competitive_landscape.difference: MPP autoregressively pretrains one transformer across heterogeneous physical systems and demonstrates transfer for multi-step surrogate prediction. The current paper tests whether its published AViT-tiny features transfer to governing-parameter regression; MPP is worse than JEPA on two systems but better on Rayleigh-Bénard, under a different end-to-end adaptation protocol and without target-system pretraining.

competitive_landscape.title: Revisiting Feature Prediction for Learning Visual Representations from Video
competitive_landscape.difference: V-JEPA establishes latent feature prediction as a stand-alone video SSL objective and evaluates large frozen representations on motion- and appearance-based natural-video tasks. This paper adapts the general principle to small scientific trajectory models, changes the encoder and loss to a 3D CNN with VICReg, and evaluates governing-parameter regression rather than video recognition.

competitive_landscape.title: VideoMAE: Masked Autoencoders are Data-Efficient Learners for Self-Supervised Video Pre-Training
competitive_landscape.difference: VideoMAE uses extreme tube masking and pixel reconstruction to learn video-transformer features, with extensive recognition, transfer, and masking-ratio evaluation. Here a small VideoMAE is trained for six epochs per physical system and used as the pixel-space comparator; the result narrows to parameter regression and does not control architecture or convergence against JEPA.

competitive_landscape.title: The Well: a Large-Scale Collection of Diverse Physics Simulations for Machine Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: The Well supplies the 15-TB, 16-dataset simulation collection and baseline infrastructure from which the three evaluated systems come. The current paper contributes a representation-learning evaluation slice and parameter-regression protocol, not new physical simulations or a broad benchmark over the entire collection.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the work presents a new perspective on physical modeling by evaluating representations on governing-parameter inference and concludes that latent prediction produces more physically informative and label-efficient features than pixel reconstruction and autoregression. Prior work already combines joint-embedding SSL with PDE coefficient regression, V-JEPA establishes latent video feature prediction, and DISCO/MPP provide the physical latent-operator and autoregressive baselines. Reviewer inference: the defensible novelty is a compact, reproducible comparison of four representation paradigms on three The Well parameter-regression tasks, plus the empirical result that a simple target-specific dynamics JEPA beats VideoMAE and MPP on two or three systems and scales better with shear-flow labels. The data do not isolate objective causality, establish general physical understanding, or support an unconditional latent-over-pixel hierarchy because architecture, exposure, adaptation, and compute differ and DISCO is uniformly strongest.
reviewer_notes: The complete nine-page workshop paper was read, including the related-work and implementation appendices. Primary competitor records were independently checked on arXiv/OpenReview. Results are transcribed at the reported precision. The paper contains no explicit limitations section and no uncertainty reporting, so the limitations list clearly labels reviewer inference. There is no direct table arithmetic contradiction; the central qualification is narrative scope: DISCO wins all three systems and MPP beats JEPA on Rayleigh-Bénard, while the conclusion groups methods as latent versus pixel despite major protocol confounds.
